question: What is the probability of emitting a 14.4 keV gamma photon at the source within 100 ns after one ordinary electronically occupied iron-57 nucleus is prepared in its 14.4 keV level?

facts.preparation: One iron-57 nucleus in its 14.41295 keV (3/2-) first excited level at time zero, with ordinary electronic occupancy and no subsequent driving or feeding.
facts.event: Source emission of the 14.4 keV nuclear photon, integrated over all directions.

evaluatedPopulationHalfLife.location: DDEP Co-57 evaluation comments, Tables 2 and 3, 14.413 keV level
evaluatedPopulationHalfLife.conversion: Divide the population half-life and its uncertainty by ln(2), then convert nanoseconds to seconds.

evaluatedTotalInternalConversionCoeffici.definition: Ratio of total internal conversion rate to gamma emission rate for the first excited level to ground-state transition.
evaluatedTotalInternalConversionCoeffici.location: DDEP Co-57 evaluated table, section 2.2, gamma(1,0)(Fe) row, alpha_T column
